Subject: Redwood Private connectivity for inference – initial ask

Sean —

We're starting an onboarding for Redwood Private (on-prem control plane talking to your inference nodes in our VPC). Security team asked for a short write-up on the recommended connectivity patterns (VPC peering vs interface endpoints / PrivateLink vs site-to-site VPN). Key constraints:
- No IP overlap allowed with our core VPCs today (large CIDR footprint).
- All traffic must be encrypted in transit; we prefer managed endpoints if they help with auditing.
- We need a pilot within 3 weeks and production within 10 weeks.
- Throughput requirement ~ 800 Mbps sustained, spiky to 2 Gbps.
- Ops wants minimal operational overhead and clearly auditable flows.

Can you sketch tradeoffs and recommend a default approach? A short pros/cons + rollout suggestion would be perfect.

Thanks,
Rajiv
Rajiv Khanna
Director, Network Engineering — FinBank

Rajiv —

Thanks for the clear constraints. Quick clarifying Qs before we draft the recommendation:
1) Which cloud provider/region will host the inference nodes (AWS us-west-2, GCP us-west1, etc)?
2) Do you control the routing/RT tables for the VPCs that will connect to our endpoints, or will that be handled by a central NetOps team?
3) Any regulatory requirement around private peering (we sometimes see orgs that forbid cross-account peering for audit reasons)?

Based on what you wrote, my upfront sense: PrivateLink (interface endpoints) gives the cleanest cross-account surface and keeps IPs decoupled, but it comes with per-GB and per-hour endpoint costs and connection quotas. VPC peering is cheap and performant but requires non-overlapping IPs and is harder to scale across many VPCs (no transitive routing). S2S VPN is fastest to stand up for pilots and provides encryption + BGP for route exchange, but it has more moving parts and operational burden.

I'll assemble a one-pager and attach a sketch and an initial cost estimate. If you can answer the three questions above, we'll tailor it.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Summary of perf/operational tradeoffs (short):

- VPC peering: lowest latency, no per-packet service hop, scales well for sustained throughput (subject to ENI/bandwidth limits); drawback = must have disjoint IP space and peering is point-to-point between VPCs (no transitive). For multi-VPC orgs you'll need many peerings or a transit VPC. Peering doesn't provide native endpoint auditing for cross-account service access.

- Interface endpoints (PrivateLink): excellent for cross-account isolation — we present a managed service interface and you keep full control of your VPC CIDR. Data path enters via an ENI in your VPC; per-GB egress and endpoint-hour charges apply. Latency adds a small hop (~1–8 ms typical), and throughput is dependent on endpoint ENI/ENI throughput caps but can be scaled by multiple endpoints. Strong fit when you want least blast radius and clear service-level ACLs.

- Site-to-site VPN (IPsec + BGP): fastest to pilot (cloud provider config + on-prem FW), encrypts traffic end-to-end, and supports dynamic route exchange. But VPN tunnels can exhibit higher jitter and lower predictable throughput; for sustained multi-Gbps you'll need multiple tunnels or a managed Direct Connect / ExpressRoute link. Operationally, VPNs require tunnel monitoring, key rotation, and firewall/NAT considerations.

Operational notes:
- If FinBank must avoid IP renumbering, PrivateLink avoids that pain.
- If you need strict packet-level auditing in your VPC, peering puts traffic directly into your routing fabric but lacks a nice per-consumer service boundary.
- For very large models and transfer of large model artifacts, consider an object-store sync via S3 (signed URLs) over a dedicated peering/transit link vs pushing heavy payloads over PrivateLink.

I'll attach a small sketch with estimated B/W and cost buckets for each option.

—Marcus
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Redwood Private connectivity for inference – initial ask

Rajiv / Elena —

Attached is a concise recommendation and a pilot plan. TL;DR recommendation:

1) Pilot (weeks 1–3): Stand up a pair of AES‑VPN tunnels between FinBank and Redwood pilot VPC. Reason: fastest to provision and validates control-plane interactions and telemetry collection end-to-end. Use BGP, advertise a narrow set of prefixes for the pilot.

2) Production (weeks 4–10): Migrate control-plane traffic to interface endpoints (PrivateLink) for cross-account isolation and auditability. For dataplane (high-throughput streaming/weights): option A = VPC peering/transit VPC if you can allocate disjoint CIDRs; option B = colocated Direct Connect/ExpressRoute or managed transit (if higher than ~1 Gbps sustained) — PrivateLink can be kept for control-plane and lower-volume telemetry.

3) Fallback/short-term: If IP renumbering is not feasible and Direct Connect isn't an option, keep an HA VPN cluster + autoscaling endpoints for capacity.

Operational checklist (short):
- Confirm target cloud & region.
- Provide a non-overlapping /28 (pilot prefixes) to advertise for pilot BGP.
- Decide who will run the transit VPC / Direct Connect circuit if chosen.
- Agree SLAs for packet loss/jitter for model streaming.

Attached: finbank-network-sketch-v1.png (logical flows), connectivity-costs-estimate.xlsx (ballpark fees).

If this looks good we'll draft a short MoM and schedule a 30-min pilot kickoff.

Regards,
Sean
